resources.string: Picture each word, then let it go
A new word every %1$d seconds, spoken by your device
This deck is no longer available
Could not prepare the words. Check that your device has an English text-to-speech voice, then tap play to try again.
Press play, lie back and close your eyes.
When you hear a word, picture it for a few seconds: its shape, its color, where it might be.
Let it go when the next word arrives. There is nothing to connect and nothing to remember.
If your thoughts drift back to your day, just wait for the next word. Set the sleep timer so the words stop on their own.
Based on research by Luc P. Beaudoin into serial diverse imagining, also known as the cognitive shuffle. Early studies are promising; it is not a medical treatment.
